steps.title: Welcome to ZaakAfhandelApp
steps.body: Let's take a quick spin through your case handling — we'll create a case together so you can see how the pieces fit. You'll add the record yourself.
Cases are the heart of the app — every task, document and decision hangs off a case. Open Cases from the menu to get started.
Add your first case — give it a case type and save. You can attach tasks, documents and decisions to it afterwards.
steps.task: Click New and save a case

steps.body: Tasks are the work items that move a case forward. Open Tasks from the menu.

steps.title: You're all set
steps.body: Nicely done — your case handling has its first case. Head back to the Dashboard to watch it grow, and reopen this tour anytime from the … menu.

config._note: CASE archetype — the operational heart of zaakgericht werken. A caseworker opens a zaak to see where it stands and what work remains, so the body leads with the case fields (status, deadlines, verantwoordelijke organisatie) 8-wide beside a Related panel, then surfaces the child collections that drive the case: open Tasks (taak.zaak=@objectId) and the case file's Documents (document.zaak=@objectId), followed by Decisions (besluit) and Results (resultaat) because closing a zaak hinges on them, and a Files leaf for the raw attachment surface. summaryAggregates give at-a-glance counts of open tasks, documents, decisions and roles. The schema declares NO email/calendar/talk linkedTypes, so no comms leaves sit on the body. ADR-049 Phase-4 dissolution assessment (updated for nextcloud-vue #89): the w3 CnObjectSidebar now resolves a per-tab widgets[].type:'object-table' to CnWidgetObjectTable and provides cnObjectContext, so besluiten — the ONE relation with a real parent-zaak-filtered endpoint (GET api/zrc/zaken/{zaakUuid}/besluiten → {results:[{url,uuid,zaak,besluit}]}, zaakUuid=@objectId) — IS now wired as an object-table sidebar tab (endpointSource url carrying @objectId in the PATH + responsePath 'results'); no whole-page migration was needed on this legacy catalog-shape detail page. The OTHER SIX stay config.sidebarTabs[].component STUBS for ENDPOINT reasons (not a renderer gap): the rollen/statussen/resultaten/zaakinformatieobjecten ZGW list controllers call CallService->index with no query forwarding so their zaak filter is dropped; taken/documenten/resultaten already render in the body via OR object-lists; berichten's bericht.zaak is unverified (relation runs through klantcontact). Per-tab detail in each tab's _note.

sidebarTabs.label: Tasks
sidebarTabs._note: STUB (ADR-049 Phase-4): parent-zaak taken already render in the detail body (widget zaak-taken). api/taken (TakenController->objectService) forwards ?zaak=@objectId (taak.zaak=@objectId proven by the body list). Not dissolved: no object-table sidebar-tab renderer in w3 CnObjectSidebar.

sidebarTabs.label: Roles
sidebarTabs._note: STUB (ADR-049 Phase-4): ZGW api/zrc/rollen exists but RollenController::index calls CallService->index with no query forwarding, so a ?zaak filter is dropped. OR api/objects/rollen?zaak=@objectId IS reachable (rol.zaak=@objectId proven by the Roles summaryAggregate). Not dissolved: no object-table sidebar-tab renderer in w3 CnObjectSidebar.

sidebarTabs.label: Documents
sidebarTabs._note: STUB (ADR-049 Phase-4): ZGW api/zrc/zaakinformatieobjecten exists but ZaakInformatieObjectenController::index calls CallService->index with no query forwarding, so a ?zaak filter is dropped. Parent-zaak documents already render in the detail body (widget zaak-documenten). Not dissolved: no object-table sidebar-tab renderer in w3 CnObjectSidebar.

sidebarTabs.label: Messages
sidebarTabs._note: STUB (ADR-049 Phase-4): api/berichten (BerichtenController->objectService) forwards request params but a bericht.zaak field is UNVERIFIED — the schema is seeded externally (not in-repo), bericht is absent from the body/summaryAggregates, and this relation runs through klantcontact, not a direct zaak field. Endpoint-not-built for a parent-zaak filter; also no object-table sidebar-tab renderer in w3 CnObjectSidebar.

sidebarTabs.label: Results
sidebarTabs._note: STUB (ADR-049 Phase-4): ZGW api/zrc/resultaten exists but ResultatenController::index calls CallService->index with no query forwarding, so a ?zaak filter is dropped. Parent-zaak results already render in the detail body (widget zaak-resultaten). Not dissolved: no object-table sidebar-tab renderer in w3 CnObjectSidebar.

sidebarTabs.label: Statuses
sidebarTabs._note: STUB (ADR-049 Phase-4): ZGW api/zrc/statussen exists but StatusenController::index calls CallService->index with no query forwarding, so a ?zaak filter is dropped; a status.zaak field is also unverified (status absent from body/summaryAggregates). Endpoint-not-built for a parent-zaak filter; also no object-table sidebar-tab renderer in w3 CnObjectSidebar.

config._note: ACTION-ITEM archetype — a single work item that moves a case forward. A handler opens a taak to see what to do, by when, and against which case, so the body leads with the task fields (status, deadline, actie, toelichting) 8-wide next to a Related panel that resolves its FKs (parent zaak, klant, medewerker, contactmoment). A Files leaf holds any working attachments. Tasks have no child collections and the schema declares NO email/calendar/talk linkedTypes, so the layout is deliberately compact — data + related + files, no comms leaves.

PERSON/ORGANISATION (relation) archetype — the 360 view of a citizen or company the municipality deals with. The body leads with identity + contact fields (naam, emailadres, telefoonnummer, address, BSN/KVK) 8-wide beside a Related panel, then surfaces this relation's history as object-lists: their Cases (zaak.klant=@objectId), Contact moments (contactmoment.klant=@objectId) and open Tasks (taak.klant=@objectId). summaryAggregates count their cases and contact moments. IMPORTANT: although this is a person/organisation, the klant schema declares NO email/calendar/talk linkedTypes, so per the hard rule NO comms leaves are placed on the body — the emailadres/telefoonnummer live as plain fields in the data widget.

EMPLOYEE (person) archetype — an internal handler's workload view. The medewerker schema is thin (naam, email, telefoonnummer), so the compact contact card sits 6-wide next to Related, and the value of the page is the two workload object-lists below: Tasks assigned to them (taak.medewerker=@objectId) and Contact moments they handled (contactmoment.medewerker=@objectId), with a summaryAggregate of open assigned tasks. Person archetype, but the schema declares NO email/calendar/talk linkedTypes so the email/phone stay as plain data fields and no comms leaves sit on the body.

INTERACTION-LOG archetype — a single logged contact (call, email, counter visit) captured against a klant/zaak. The record's whole value is the note plus who/when/which-channel, so the body is a wide 3-column data widget (notitie, kanaal, startDate, status) with a Related panel that resolves its FKs (klant, zaak, taak, medewerker) so the handler can jump to the case or customer. No child collections; the contactmoment schema declares NO email/calendar/talk linkedTypes (the channel/date are plain fields), so no comms leaves — the layout is intentionally minimal: data + related.

MESSAGE/CORRESPONDENCE archetype — a single message (onderwerp + berichttekst/inhoud) exchanged with a customer, with a bijlage attachment type. The body puts the message content front-and-centre in a wide data widget (onderwerp, berichttekst, berichtType, publicatieDatum) with a Related panel for its context, and a Files leaf below for the actual attachment surface (bijlageType indicates enclosures). The bericht schema declares NO email/calendar/talk linkedTypes — the message text is stored data, not a live mailbox thread — so no email leaf is placed; Files is included because messages carry attachments.

ROLE / PARTY-IN-CASE archetype — a junction record binding a betrokkene (person/organisation) to a zaak in a specific capacity (initiator, behandelaar, belanghebbende…). The body is data-led (roltype, omschrijvingGeneriek, betrokkeneType, contactpersoonRol, roltoelichting) 8-wide beside a Related panel that resolves the linked zaak and the betrokkene so a handler can navigate both sides of the relationship. It has no child collections and the schema declares NO comms linkedTypes, so the layout is deliberately minimal: data + related, no files or comms leaves.

CATALOG/TEMPLATE (config) archetype — the definition of a case type (doel, aanleiding, doorlooptijd, servicenorm, publication settings, validity dates). This is a configuration record with many attributes, so the body uses a wide 3-column data widget to show the full definition, a Related panel for its catalogus/selectielijst links, and — the key operational payoff — an object-list of Cases created from this type (zaak.zaaktype=@objectId) with a summaryAggregate count. NO comms/files leaves: a zaaktype is a template, it doesn't communicate or carry attachments.

DECISION-DOCUMENT archetype — the formal besluit that (often) closes a case. The schema is thin (besluit, url, zaak), so the compact data card sits beside a Related panel that resolves the parent zaak, and the page gives prominence to the Files leaf: a besluit is a legal document and its attachment/PDF is the artefact people come to read. NO comms leaves (a decision doesn't hold a mailbox) — the document itself is the focus, so Files spans full width below the header row.

DOCUMENT archetype — a ZGW enkelvoudig informatieobject. The whole point of the page is the file plus its rich records-management metadata, so the layout is document-first: the Files leaf takes a prominent 8-wide column (open/preview the actual content), with the metadata data widget (titel, auteur, status, vertrouwelijkheidaanduiding, versie, ondertekening, integriteit, informatieobjecttype) 4-wide beside it, and a Related panel resolving the parent zaak below. NO comms leaves — a document is an artefact, not a conversation.

OUTCOME archetype — the resultaat classifies how a case ended (resultaattype + toelichting) and feeds the archiving/selectielijst regime. The schema is intentionally thin, so the page is deliberately minimal: a data widget (resultaattype, toelichting) beside a Related panel that resolves the parent zaak. No child collections, no attachments to speak of, and NO comms linkedTypes — a result is a classification, so data + related is the right, honest layout rather than padding it with empty leaves.

STATUS-EVENT archetype — a single entry in a case's status timeline (statustype, datum, statustoelichting). It is one immutable point in the zaak's history, so the page is intentionally minimal: a data widget showing the status entry beside a Related panel that resolves the parent zaak so the reader can jump back to the full timeline on the case. No children, no attachments, NO comms linkedTypes — padding a single timeline event with leaves would be dishonest, so data + related is exactly right.
